title: What Is an AI SDR? A Practical Guide for Sales Teams in 2026
summary: Learn what an AI SDR is, how it works, where it fits in outbound sales, and how teams should evaluate AI SDR software in 2026.
body_text: An AI SDR is software that automates or augments parts of the sales development workflow—research, outreach, calling, qualification, follow-up, and CRM updates. It is most effective as an assistive layer that gives human reps leverage: less time on repetitive work, more time on high-judgment conversations. This guide explains what AI SDRs are, how they work, where they fit, what they should and should not do, and how to evaluate platforms. If you are comparing tools, see Trellus’s buyer guide to AI SDR software . What is an AI SDR? An AI SDR applies artificial intelligence to SDR tasks across prospecting and early-funnel engagement. It can research accounts, prioritize leads, draft messages, support calls, summarize conversations, qualify replies, and keep systems up to date. Simple definition: An AI SDR is software that helps sales teams find, contact, qualify, and follow up with potential buyers more efficiently. Think leverage, not replacement. Humans still own strategy, ICP and messaging judgment, complex discovery, objection handling, relationship building, and deal progression. Why AI SDRs matter in 2026 Hitting pipeline targets is harder: response rates are lower, data is messy, and leaders expect personalization without losing volume. AI SDRs emerged to reduce manual work while preserving relevance and compliance. Common adoption drivers: •Excessive manual research •Slow speed to lead on inbound or intent-driven prospects •Inconsistent follow-up and logging •Low connect rates on phone •New reps needing structure during live conversations •Limited manager visibility into calls, messaging, and next steps AI does not fix a weak list or unclear messaging. With sound data, guardrails, and process, it improves speed and consistency. AI SDR meaning: what the term includes and excludes Vendors use “AI SDR” to describe everything from autonomous agents to assistive dialers. Ignore labels; evaluate the workflow. What it may include: •Account/contact research •Lead scoring or prioritization •Email and message drafting •Call prep, talk tracks, and live suggestions •Dialing support; voicemail and call summaries •Objection-handling recommendations •Reply classification, qualification, and routing •CRM updates, task creation, and follow-up generation What it typically does not replace: •ICP and territory design •Messaging strategy and legal review •Enterprise discovery and negotiation •Relationship management and sales leadership judgment For broader workflow design, see our guide to AI for sales prospecting . How an AI SDR works AI SDRs blend data inputs, models, workflow automation, human review, and integrations. A common flow: 1.Input data: accounts, contacts, history, CRM fields, intent, notes. 2.Interpretation: summarize context; classify fit and urgency. 3.Recommendation or execution: draft messages, suggest call angles, trigger tasks, log notes. 4.Human review: reps or managers approve or edit where judgment matters. 5.Learning loop: replies, connects, meetings, and dispositions inform updates. They work best when teams define audiences, guardrails, approval points, and success metrics. AI SDR vs. human SDR vs. traditional sales automation AI SDRs sit between human judgment and rule-based automation—able to interpret and draft, but still needing constraints. What Is an AI SDR? A Practical Guide for Sales Teams in 2026 — Table 1 Category What it does well Where it struggles Best use Human SDR Judgment, empathy, live discovery, account nuance, relationship building Repetitive admin, high-volume research, manual logging, inconsistent follow-up Complex conversations, strategic accounts, qualification, objection handling Traditional sales automation Repeatable sequences, task reminders, routing, structured workflows Personalization, adaptive reasoning, unstructured data interpretation Enforcing process, scaling known workflows, maintaining cadence AI SDR Research assistance, message drafting, call support, prioritization, summaries, workflow acceleration Requires oversight, depends on data quality, may misread nuance, can create risk without guardrails Helping reps execute faster and more consistently across prospecting and follow-up Adoption is strongest when AI complements the team rather than replacing the motion. What tasks can an AI SDR handle? Capabilities vary by platform. Verify current features before buying. Prospect and account research AI summarizes company context, likely pain points, relevant triggers, and suggested openers. Reps should validate details before referencing them. Lead prioritization Models rank accounts based on fit and engagement signals. Compare AI rankings to real outcomes to catch bias or gaps. Message drafting and personalization AI drafts first touches, follow-ups, objection replies, and LinkedIn notes. Use approved frameworks and require rep review—especially when referencing a prospect’s business. Calling support AI helps with call prep, dialing workflows, talk tracks, live prompts, summaries, and next steps. Useful for new reps and coaching. For the broader assistant category, see our guide to AI sales assistants . Qualification and routing AI classifies replies, detects intent or objections, and recommends AE routing. Keep human checks for complex deals. CRM updates and admin AI generates summaries, fills fields, creates tasks, and standardizes dispositions. Cleaner data improves follow-up and reporting. What an AI SDR should not do without oversight Increase governance as autonomy increases. Be cautious about allowing AI to: •Send large volumes of unreviewed personalized outreach •Make unsupported claims or reference unverified prospect details •Handle sensitive data without proper controls •Ignore consent, opt-out, or regional communication rules •Make qualification or routing decisions with no review •Update critical CRM fields without auditability •Represent itself unclearly in buyer-facing interactions Start human-in-the-loop; expand autonomy only after quality is proven. Where AI SDRs fit in the sales organization •Outbound SDRs: Research, call prep, drafting, prioritization, follow-up discipline. •Inbound qualification: Faster response, summarization of form context, routing, and next-step recommendations. •BDRs: Multichannel orchestration similar to SDRs. •AEs: Pre-meeting research, follow-up drafting, and expansion prospecting (with more account nuance). •Sales managers: Summaries and conversation insights to target coaching. Benefits and limitations of AI SDRs Benefits: •Faster prospect preparation •More consistent follow-up and documentation •Better manager leverage via summaries and insights •Smoother onboarding with prompts and structure •Reduced admin through automated logging Limitations: •Highly dependent on data quality and list fit •Risk of generic or inaccurate messaging without strong prompts •Potential misinterpretation of context; reps must verify key details •Requires intentional workflow and guardrails to perform well How to evaluate an AI SDR platform Start with your motion, not vendor labels. 1) What workflow are you improving first? Pick a clear bottleneck: slow call prep, inconsistent follow-up, incomplete CRM notes, delayed inbound response, or limited coaching visibility. A focused use case makes measurement straightforward. 2) Does the platform match your channel mix? Tools often lean email-heavy, call-heavy, or multichannel. If the phone is central, assess call prep, dialing support, live prompts, summaries, and coaching workflows. For email, review personalization controls, approvals, deliverability, and reply handling. 3) How much autonomy do you want? Assistive models keep reps in control; more autonomous models execute steps directly. More autonomy can speed results but demands tighter governance and monitoring. 4) Can managers inspect and improve the workflow? Avoid black boxes. Managers should see recommendations, approvals, and outcomes; they need levers for experimentation, QA, and coaching. 5) How does it fit your existing stack? Confirm current integrations with your CRM, sales engagement, dialer, data providers, calendar, and conversation intelligence. Depth matters: surface-level syncs won’t support full workflows. For a broader selection framework, see how to choose AI SDR software . AI SDR implementation: a practical rollout plan Step 1: Define the target use case Choose one workflow (e.g., “improve cold call preparation”). Establish a baseline: prep time, call volume, connect rate, common objections, CRM gaps. Step 2: Create guardrails Document approved value props, sensitive claims requiring sign-off, allowed data sources, and actions that require human review. Step 3: Pilot with a small team Select a few reps and one manager. Prioritize users who will follow the process and give actionable feedback. Step 4: Review quality, not just quantity Inspect message samples, call recordings, qualification notes, and CRM updates. More activity is not success if relevance declines. Step 5: Expand gradually Scale to adjacent use cases only after the first workflow is stable. Update prompts, playbooks, and permissions as you learn. Common AI SDR use cases •Cold outbound: Draft first touches, call openers, and structured follow-ups. Works best with a clear ICP and high-quality lists. •Speed to lead: Summarize inbound context, elevate high-fit accounts, and recommend immediate next steps. •Re-engagement: Surface dormant accounts, summarize past interactions, and draft context-aware re-openers. •Event follow-up: Segment attendees, tailor follow-ups, and prioritize call lists. Keep human review due to varied intent. •Coaching and enablement: Use summaries and insights to spot skill gaps and reinforce best practices. What makes a good AI SDR workflow? A strong workflow answers: 1.Who should be contacted? 2.What information can AI use? 3.What action happens next? 4.Where does human review occur? 5.How will success be measured? Specificity reduces risk. Example: “For Tier 2 accounts, AI drafts a first-touch email using approved value props plus CRM industry and account notes. Reps must review before sending. Managers audit reply quality weekly.” How AI SDRs affect SDR roles AI shifts the role from manual execution to judgment and conversation quality. High performers get better at: •Editing AI drafts and validating insights •Choosing channels and timing •Running stronger live conversations •Interpreting buyer intent and advancing next steps •Giving feedback that improves prompts and workflows •Using data to refine outreach Managers should coach how reps use and override AI—and whether AI is improving buyer interactions. AI SDR metrics to track Avoid activity-only dashboards. Blend leading and lagging indicators: •Research/prep time •Quality conversations •Connect-to-meeting conversion •Positive reply rate and reply quality •Follow-up completion and speed to lead •CRM completion rate and data accuracy •Meeting show rate •Qualified pipeline sourced •Manager-reviewed call/message quality Questions to ask vendors •Which SDR workflows are supported today? •Which features are assistive vs. autonomous? •How does the platform use CRM and activity data? •What integrations are available now? •Can managers control approved messaging and prompts? •Can reps review and edit AI-generated outreach before sending? •How are call notes, summaries, and dispositions created? •What reporting and QA tools do managers get? •How are opt-outs, consent, and regional rules handled? •What data trains or improves the system? •What implementation support is included? •How should we measure success in the first 30–90 days? Request a demo using realistic data to confirm workflow fit. Where Trellus fits Trellus is built for teams adopting AI-assisted outbound—especially where live calling, rep execution, and coaching matter. Explore the Trellus AI SDR to support a sales development motion that keeps reps focused on conversations while AI assists with repetitive or time-sensitive tasks. As with any platform, confirm current features, integrations, onboarding needs, and plan details before purchase. Fit depends on team size, channel mix, process, and desired autonomy. Conclusion An AI SDR helps teams research, reach out, qualify, follow up, and keep systems current. It is a leverage layer—not a replacement—for human SDRs. Start with a specific workflow, define guardrails, run a focused pilot, and measure quality as well as speed. Ready to explore whether Trellus fits your motion? Learn more about the AI SDR platform , start a free trial if available, or request a demo. FAQ What is an AI SDR? Software that uses AI to assist with SDR tasks such as research, outreach, call support, qualification, follow-up, and CRM updates. What does AI SDR stand for? Artificial intelligence sales development representative—usually software that performs or assists with parts of the SDR workflow. Is an AI SDR the same as a human SDR? No. Humans provide judgment, empathy, discovery, and relationship building. AI assists with repetitive and data-heavy tasks. Can an AI SDR make cold calls? Some platforms support calling workflows (prep, dialing assistance, prompts, summaries, or AI voice interactions). Verify exact capabilities and compliance before use. Will AI replace SDRs? AI may automate tasks, but most B2B teams still need human sellers for strategy, judgment, and conversations. Treat AI as a productivity and consistency layer. What is the difference between an AI SDR and an AI sales assistant? An AI SDR focuses on prospecting and early qualification. An AI sales assistant is broader, supporting SDRs, AEs, managers, and other sales tasks. How should a team start using an AI SDR? Pick one use case, define guardrails, run a small pilot, review quality, and expand after results are consistent. What should buyers verify before choosing an AI SDR tool? Current features, integrations, data handling, compliance controls, reporting, implementation support, and plan details.

title: What Are the Best Qvidian Alternatives in 2026?
summary: Qvidian alternatives compared on portal coverage, pricing transparency and time to value. 166 G2 reviews, 4-month implementation, and who fits which job.
body_text: ‍ Last updated: August 2026 ‍ The best Qvidian alternative depends on which of three jobs you are replacing: proposal production, security questionnaire response, or DDQ cycles. For proposal-led teams the closest like-for-like replacements are Responsive and Loopio; for questionnaire and DDQ volume the AI-native options are AutoRFP, Conveyor, Skypher, and Wolfia; for government and defence proposals AutogenAI is the only one holding FedRAMP High. ‍ Qvidian itself remains a reasonable choice if your requirement is regulatory audit depth rather than automation speed, and this article says where that is true. ‍ We make Skypher, one of the tools below. The methodology is stated so you can check we applied it to ourselves the same way, and our section names our own gaps. ‍ How we evaluated these tools Seven criteria, applied identically to every tool including Skypher. ‍ Portal coverage. Whether the vendor's own integration documentation lists third-party risk portals such as OneTrust, ServiceNow, Archer, ProcessUnity or Whistic. Checked against each vendor's published integrations page, not their marketing claims. This criterion carries weight because 19.2% of security questionnaires arrive through portals , against 71.2% Excel and 9.6% Word, across 100,000+ questions processed through Skypher. ‍ Pricing transparency. Whether a figure is published on the vendor's own site. Prices quoted in competitors' comparison articles were not accepted as sources. ‍ Knowledge model. Whether the tool requires a curated question-and-answer library that someone maintains, or reads existing source documents. ‍ Time to value. Published implementation data where it exists. G2 aggregates this from real users for some tools and not others. ‍ Independent review evidence. G2 rating and review volume. Volume matters as much as the score. ‍ Scope. Which of RFPs, security questionnaires and DDQs the tool actually covers. ‍ Format handling. Excel with macros and conditional logic, Word with tables, PDFs, and portal-based submission. ‍ Where we could not verify something from a primary source, it is marked "not verified" rather than assumed absent. ‍ Qvidian and its alternatives compared ‍ Tool Public pricing Portals in published integrations Knowledge model G2 Upland Qvidian No public pricing None listed Curated library 4.3 (166) Responsive (RFPIO) No public pricing Not verified Curated library 4.5 Loopio No public pricing Not verified Curated library 4.7 AutogenAI No public pricing Not verified Bespoke language engine 4.4 AutoRFP $899/mo Scale, $1,299/mo Accelerate Not verified Source documents 4.8 Conveyor From $9,600/yr Business Yes Knowledge base 4.6 (150) Skypher No public pricing Yes, 40+ Source documents 4.9, low volume Wolfia No public pricing Yes, 45+ claimed Source documents Not rated 1up Not verified Not verified Live connectors 4.9 Arphie No public pricing Not verified Live source systems 4.9 ‍ Pricing verified on vendor sites in August 2026. Qvidian's absence of portal integrations was confirmed independently on both uplandsoftware.com/qvidian/integrations and its G2 listing. ‍ This table is scoped to tools a Qvidian user would realistically move to. For a wider view of the category, including SafeBase, SecurityPal and Vanta, see our roundup of the best security questionnaire automation software . ‍ Staying on Upland Qvidian: Rating: 4.3 from 166 G2 reviews. 156 of those are four or five stars, so most users are satisfied. Qvidian is Upland Software's proposal platform, with nearly 50 years of heritage, 200,000+ users, 8 of the 10 largest US banks, 6 of the 10 largest European banks and 4 of the 5 largest asset management firms. Reviewers praise the content library, version control, Microsoft Office integration and a support team they thank by name. Genuine weakness: G2's aggregated user data puts implementation at 4 months and return on investment at 16 months. Reviewers describe AI Assist as "just a simple index search" and ask for "automated first draft generation". One enterprise financial services reviewer writes that the UI "seem[s] more like legacy software than a modern SaaS platform". The published integration list contains no third-party risk portals. Stay if your requirement is regulatory audit depth, approval chains and version control on formal proposals, and your questionnaires arrive as files rather than portal links Proposal-led Qvidian alternatives AutogenAI Builds a bespoke language model per customer trained on your own proposals and win themes, so drafts carry your voice from the start. The only tool here with FedRAMP High , which for US federal work handling controlled unclassified information is a procurement requirement rather than a preference. G2 4.4. ‍ Genuine weakness: no public pricing, minimum seat commitments and onboarding fees. Not built for high-volume questionnaire or DDQ work, so teams doing both need a second tool. Loopio Cleaner interface than Qvidian with a well-governed content library and a 9.7 out of 10 G2 support score. G2 4.7. For teams whose main complaint about Qvidian is adoption friction among occasional contributors, this is the smallest change that fixes it. ‍ Genuine weakness: the same curated library model underneath, so the maintenance burden that frustrates Qvidian teams carries over. No public pricing. AI was added to an existing platform rather than built in. Responsive (RFPIO) The deepest integration ecosystem in the category, with mature analytics and broad procurement portal connectivity. G2 4.5. The closest structural match to what Qvidian actually does. ‍ Genuine weakness: shares Qvidian's architecture, so teams leaving because of AI quality find the same ceiling. G2 reviewers flag navigation complexity for occasional contributors. No public pricing, and seat-based costs create the same friction when you loop in reviewers. ‍ Qvidian alternatives for RFPs, questionnaires and DDQs AutoRFP Publishes pricing openly at $899 a month for Scale and $1,299 for Accelerate, both with unlimited users, plus a 30-day money-back guarantee. G2 4.8. Meaningful investment in DDQ content for fund managers, with ILPA, AIMA and ESG DDQ material published. ‍ Genuine weakness: a response acceleration tool rather than a full bid-lifecycle platform, so capture planning, bid/no-bid scoring and compliance matrix generation are outside its scope. Younger ecosystem than Qvidian, with less enterprise deployment history. Skypher Reads existing documents rather than requiring a curated library: past questionnaires, SOC 2 reports, policies, and connected sources including SharePoint, Google Drive and Confluence. 40+ portal integrations covering OneTrust, ServiceNow, Archer and Coupa. Three answer styles plus per-answer rewording, role-based access control, multi-language handling. Adobe, Deel and McKinsey are customers. ‍ Genuine weakness: no public pricing, so you cannot build a business case without a call. Our G2 review volume is low against Qvidian's 166 and Conveyor's 150, which is fair to hold against us. No contract redlining, which Wolfia has. On portal count Wolfia claims 45+ against our 40+, so we lose that comparison. ‍ Security-questionnaire-led Qvidian alternatives Conveyor Publishes pricing from $9,600 a year for the Business tier with unlimited seats, which makes it the easiest tool here to budget against without a sales call. G2 4.6 from 150 reviews, with support praised in review after review. Named customers include Atlassian, Zendesk, Carta and Zapier. ‍ Genuine weakness: credit-based metering on both trust center access and questionnaires, which bites when volume is unpredictable. G2 reviewers report rewriting correct answers because "the tone is still not up to par", and request wider portal compatibility. Note that Conveyor also advertises unlimited seats and publishes 96% answer accuracy, the same figure Skypher publishes, so neither is a point of difference between us. Our full Conveyor review has the detail. Wolfia Built around a source citation on every answer with hallucination-prevention checks before responses leave the system. Adds a Contract Review Agent for security addenda, which nothing else here does. Named customers include Amplitude, Miro, Instacart and CircleCI, with published results such as 90% automation and sub-two-day turnaround at Handshake. ‍ Genuine weakness: no G2 rating at all as of 2026, so there is no independent review evidence to check. UpGuard's category comparison identifies the main limitation as "months of feeding corrections and authoritative answers before reaching high automation". No public pricing. Our full Wolfia review covers it. ‍ Lightweight Qvidian alternatives 1up Surfaces answers inside Slack, Teams and Google Chat, so contributors work in tools they already use and there is effectively no learning curve. G2 4.9. A free plan exists. ‍ Genuine weakness: not built for complex multi-document proposal workflows with review gates and multi-stakeholder coordination. Teams needing both a questionnaire tool and a proposal platform will still need two. Arphie Connects AI agents to live source systems including SharePoint, Confluence, Notion and Google Drive, so answers reflect current documents with no parallel library to curate. Confidence scores and citations on every answer. G2 4.9. ‍ Genuine weakness: removing the library does not remove knowledge governance. Disorganised SharePoint produces disorganised answers, so the maintenance burden shifts rather than disappears. No public pricing. ‍ Which problem are you actually solving? Match the reason Qvidian stopped working to the shortlist. The wrong category wastes an evaluation cycle. ‍ "Our AI does not draft, it just searches." Your reviewers are describing an architecture, not a setting. Look at tools built after 2023: AutoRFP, Conveyor, Skypher, Wolfia, Arphie. Loopio and Responsive share Qvidian's underlying model and will not fix this. "We spend more time maintaining the library than answering." You need a tool that reads source documents rather than curated Q&A pairs: Arphie, AutoRFP, Skypher, Wolfia. "Half our questionnaires arrive as portal links." Verify portal coverage against the vendor's own integration documentation before anything else. Conveyor, Skypher and Wolfia publish portal integrations. Qvidian does not. "We cannot model the cost." Only AutoRFP and Conveyor publish figures. Everyone else here, Skypher included, requires a sales conversation. "Contributors will not adopt it." Loopio for the smallest change, 1up if your contributors live in Slack. "We need FedRAMP High." AutogenAI. Nothing else here qualifies. "Our requirement is audit trails and approval governance for regulated financial services." Stay on Qvidian, or run it alongside a specialist for the questionnaire queue. This is a genuine strength of theirs that the AI-native tools have not matched, and replacing it carries real risk. Whichever way that lands, test it on a real questionnaire rather than a prepared demo. Send each shortlisted vendor an actual file you struggled with, in its original format, and compare what comes back. If you want to run that test with us, you can book a demo,,, . Adobe went from two weeks to two hours per questionnaire. ‍ FAQ What is the best Qvidian alternative for enterprise proposal teams? Responsive and Loopio are the closest like-for-like replacements, since both cover proposal production, content governance and multi-contributor workflows the way Qvidian does. Responsive has the deeper integration ecosystem; Loopio has the cleaner interface and a 9.7 out of 10 G2 support score. Neither publishes pricing, and both share Qvidian's curated-library model, so neither solves the AI architecture complaint. How much does Qvidian cost, and which alternatives publish pricing? Qvidian does not publish pricing; it is custom enterprise pricing within the Upland Software portfolio. G2's aggregated user data reports 4 months to implement, 16 months to return on investment, and an average discount of 7%. Two alternatives publish figures on their own sites: AutoRFP at $899 a month for Scale and $1,299 for Accelerate, and Conveyor from $9,600 a year for Business. Loopio, Responsive, AutogenAI, Wolfia, Arphie and Skypher all require a sales conversation. Does Qvidian handle security questionnaires and DDQs? It markets both, and DDQ writers on G2 confirm using it for annual cycles where the same questions repeat, describing the template linking as a real time-saver. The constraint is portal coverage: Qvidian's published integrations on both its own site and its G2 listing contain no third-party risk portals, so questionnaires arriving through OneTrust, ServiceNow or Archer have no native path in. Across 100,000+ questions processed through Skypher, 19.2% of security questionnaires arrive through portals. Should I replace Qvidian or run something alongside it? If you chose Qvidian for audit trails and approval governance in a regulated industry, those remain genuine strengths and replacing them carries risk. Several teams keep Qvidian for formal proposals and regulatory workflow, and run a specialist for the security questionnaire and DDQ queue. Full replacement makes more sense when questionnaires are the majority of the volume and formal proposals are occasional. Can I migrate a Qvidian content library to another platform? Most platforms accept structured exports. The better question is whether you should move all of it, since a library carrying stale or duplicated entries reproduces the same problem elsewhere. A common approach is identifying the fifth of the library that generates most of the reuse, retiring the rest, and migrating only verified content. Tools that read source documents directly rather than requiring a curated database avoid the migration question. How long does it take to get value from these tools? G2 reports 4 months to implement Qvidian and 16 months to return on investment. Comparable published figures do not exist for most alternatives, so ask each vendor directly what the first questionnaire looks like versus the tenth. For Wolfia, UpGuard's comparison notes it can take "months of feeding corrections" before automation rates climb. Tools that read existing documents rather than requiring a curated library generally produce a usable first draft sooner, though output quality still depends on how well organised your source material is. ‍

Why API Discovery Is Critical for Modern AppSec Programs
summary: Attackers map your APIs before you do. Shadow and forgotten endpoints create untested exposure. Learn how continuous API discovery closes the gap before it becomes a breach
body_text: Table of Contents Why API Inventory is Hard and Why Manual Lists Fail Continuous API Discovery For AppSec Teams See the API Discovery Map Infographic below to learn how to close the API Discovery Gap. Closing the API discovery gap with TotalAppSec Find the APIs you did not know you had. Run discovery in your own estate. Hidden API Estate And AI-speed Recon Are Reshaping Modern Application Risk Key Takeaways Unknown APIs create unattributed exposure , and such exposure rarely gets tested. Attackers build their own inventory through live reconnaissance; they do not wait for your spreadsheet. API discovery must pull from gateways, cloud, specs, traffic paths, scanners, and external exposure signals. OWASP API Top 10 includes improper inventory management because endpoint sprawl is now a core API risk. Qualys TotalAppSec helps shift from assumed inventory to a live, attributed, testable API catalog . Most Application Security Programs Begin with a List A spreadsheet. A CMDB export. A backlog from engineering. A set of URLs submitted for quarterly scanning. A few API specs from teams mature enough to publish them. It feels organized, but it carries one dangerous assumption: that the list represents what is running. Attackers Do Not Make That Assumption They enumerate. They crawl. They inspect responses, headers, paths, parameters, tokens, redirects, specs, mobile traffic, gateway behaviour, and forgotten staging routes. They do not need your target list because they can build their own. In the AI era, that process is getting faster. Verizon’s 2026 DBIR notes that 31% of breaches now start with software vulnerabilities and that threat actors are using generative AI to work faster across attack stages. That Is Why the API Discovery Gap Matters APIs are no longer a small subset of the application estate. They are the connective tissue between web apps, mobile apps, SaaS platforms, partners, AI services, cloud workloads, payment systems, identity providers, and internal business workflows. A single customer journey may touch a web front end, five internal APIs, a third-party enrichment service, a payment API, a notification API, and a model endpoint. Some of those paths are documented. Some are not. Some were created by teams that no longer own them. The risk is not just that an API exists. The risk is that nobody knows whether it is still used, whether it exposes sensitive data, whether it follows the OpenAPI spec, whether it has broken object-level authorization, or whether it sits behind a load balancer that AppSec never scoped for testing. OWASP highlights improper API inventory management because APIs tend to expose more endpoints than traditional web applications, making up-to-date documentation and deployed-version inventory essential. And for AppSec leaders, this changes the operating model. Can you find the APIs attackers will find? Can you assign ownership? Can you test what you discovered? Can discovery drive action rather than reporting? Why API Inventory is Hard and Why Manual Lists Fail A scanner-only program asks, “Did we test the apps we know about?” A discovery-first program asks, “What is actually live, who owns it, and is it testable?” The second question is harder, the one CISOs need to answer when the board asks about the application risk. Manual inventory cannot keep up with modern application delivery, where API gateways introduce new routes, cloud teams publish services directly, and mergers bring in inherited endpoints. Developers add to the gap by using Postman collections and Swagger files that never make it into central governance, and AI adoption adds another layer on top: applications now call model APIs, expose AI-backed workflows, and connect to agentic services that security teams may not yet track. Continuous API Discovery For AppSec Teams A catalog is only as good as its sources. It should combine gateway discovery, web app scanning, cloud context, internet-facing exposure, internal asset signals, third-party specs, Postman collections, Burp findings, and traffic-based intelligence where available. Any single source produces a partial list, and a partial list is indistinguishable from a complete one until an attacker proves otherwise. Every discovered API needs an owner and a test path. Discovery tells you an endpoint exists. It does not tell you whose backlog a finding lands in. An unattributed API produces findings nobody is accountable for closing, which is why orphaned endpoints often remain exposed longer than owned ones. Attribution is what converts a discovered endpoint into a remediable one. Inventory determines test scope . Anything missing from inventory is missing from scanning, compliance evidence, and risk prioritization. An endpoint that is cataloged but not testable is still, operationally, an untested endpoint. That is why discovery cannot stop at inventory: a list you cannot act on has not reduced exposure. See the API Discovery Map Infographic below to learn how to close the API Discovery Gap. Closing the API discovery gap with TotalAppSec This is where Qualys TotalAppSec fits, and it is worth measuring against those three requirements rather than a feature list. On discovery , Qualys TotalAppSec is designed to find known, unknown, rogue, shadow, and forgotten web applications and APIs, not just test what was submitted to it. On attribution , it brings web app, API, malware, risk, and remediation context into one workflow, so discovered endpoints are easier to associate with the right application, owner, risk score, and remediation path instead of living as isolated findings in separate tools. On testability , discovered APIs move straight into testing for OWASP web and API risks , OpenAPI v3 compliance, PII exposure, and malware threats. The catalog is the test scope, not a document about the test scope. The strategic shift is simple: stop treating API inventory as an administrative artifact. Treat it as a security control. Because the API you do not know about is not just missing from a report. It is missing from testing, ownership, remediation, compliance evidence, and risk scoring. Your attackers will still find it. title: Ebola Alert in Kinshasa: Nearly 200 Boat Passengers Quarantined After Suspected Case
summary: Health officials in the Democratic Republic of Congo have launched urgent monitoring efforts after a suspected Ebola-related death involving a passenger who travelled by boat toward Kinshasa. body_text: Health officials in the Democratic Republic of Congo have launched urgent monitoring efforts after a suspected Ebola-related death involving a passenger who travelled by boat toward Kinshasa. Nearly 200 people who were on board the vessel have been placed under quarantine while authorities conduct tests and track possible exposure. The incident has raised concerns because the passenger travelled from an area affected by the Ebola outbreak before reaching the region near Congo’s capital city. Although no confirmed Ebola cases have been reported in Kinshasa linked to this incident, officials are taking precautionary measures to prevent any possible spread. According to health authorities, the boat had been travelling along the Congo River for almost three weeks with around 200 passengers. After one traveller became seriously ill and later died, medical teams began identifying and monitoring everyone who may have been exposed. Authorities Take Immediate Action After Suspected Ebola Death Health officials said the passenger became sick after travelling from Pimu in Mongala Province, an area located hundreds of miles away from Kinshasa. The individual later died after showing symptoms consistent with Ebola infection. Dr Jean Kaseya, Director-General of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, said authorities decided to quarantine passengers even if some people showed no symptoms. The move was designed to ensure that possible infections were detected early. Ebola can have an incubation period where infected individuals may not immediately show signs of illness. Monitoring exposed people helps health teams identify cases before further transmission occurs. The quarantine process includes testing passengers, observing symptoms, and collecting health information. Officials are also continuing contact tracing efforts to identify anyone else who may have interacted with the suspected case. Why the Situation Has Caused Concern The latest Ebola situation has attracted attention because Kinshasa is one of Africa’s largest cities, with millions of residents. A major outbreak reaching a densely populated area could create significant challenges for health services. However, health experts have stressed that there is currently no confirmed Ebola transmission in Kinshasa from this incident. The quarantine measures are preventive and are intended to reduce risks. Ebola is a serious viral disease that spreads through direct contact with infected bodily fluids, including blood and other body substances. It can also spread through contaminated materials such as clothing, bedding, and medical equipment. Symptoms can include fever, tiredness, muscle pain, weakness, vomiting, diarrhoea, and in severe cases, internal or external bleeding. Early medical attention and infection control measures are essential for reducing fatalities and preventing wider transmission. Congo’s Ongoing Battle With Ebola The Democratic Republic of Congo has experienced repeated Ebola outbreaks over several decades. Health authorities have developed significant experience in responding to the virus through vaccination programmes, contact tracing, isolation procedures, and community awareness campaigns. The current outbreak has created additional challenges because some affected areas are difficult to reach. Conflict, limited infrastructure, and population movement have complicated efforts to monitor and contain infections. Health officials have warned that many new cases are being identified outside known contact groups. This makes tracking transmission chains more difficult because people who were not previously identified as exposed may become infected. Medical organisations working in affected areas have also raised concerns about the speed of transmission and the need for stronger access to communities. The Importance of Quarantine During Ebola Outbreaks Quarantine is one of the most important tools used during infectious disease emergencies. It allows health teams to observe people who may have been exposed and quickly provide care if symptoms develop. For the passengers travelling on the Congo River boat, quarantine does not mean that everyone is infected. Instead, it is a safety measure designed to protect both the individuals involved and the wider population. During quarantine, health workers can monitor temperature changes, assess symptoms, conduct laboratory testing, and provide medical support if required. Public health experts say early detection remains one of the strongest methods for controlling Ebola outbreaks. Identifying infections quickly can help prevent additional transmission and improve treatment outcomes. Community Awareness Remains Essential Authorities are also encouraging communities to remain alert and follow official health guidance. People are advised to avoid contact with bodily fluids from individuals who may be infected and to seek medical care if symptoms appear. Misinformation can create additional problems during disease outbreaks. Clear communication from health agencies helps communities understand actual risks and avoid unnecessary panic. Health workers continue to play a critical role by providing testing, education, vaccination where appropriate, and emergency support. What Happens Next The passengers under quarantine will continue to be monitored while health teams await test results. Authorities are also investigating the movements of the deceased passenger to determine whether additional people may have been exposed. The situation remains under close observation, particularly because of the potential impact of Ebola reaching a major population centre like Kinshasa. While the incident has created public concern, health officials say the response measures are designed to contain any possible spread at an early stage. International health organisations and local authorities will continue working together to track cases, support communities, and strengthen outbreak control efforts. Source reference: Daily Express and statements attributed to Congo health authorities and Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. Disclaimer: This article is intended for informational purposes only and does not replace advice from medical professionals or official public health agencies. Readers should rely on verified updates from recognised health authorities for the latest information about Ebola risks and safety guidance.

title: Lightning Strike During Thai Football Match Claims Player’s Life, Highlights Growing Need for Weather Safety Awareness
summary: A local football match in southern Thailand turned into a tragic scene after a sudden lightning strike hit the pitch, killing a young footballer and injuring several other players. body_text: A local football match in southern Thailand turned into a tragic scene after a sudden lightning strike hit the pitch, killing a young footballer and injuring several other players. The incident has raised concerns about the dangers of playing outdoor sports during unstable weather conditions and serves as a reminder of how quickly severe weather can become life threatening. The incident happened during the Golok FA Cup tournament at Santiphap Stadium in Sungai Golok, Narathiwat province, southern Thailand. The match was being played between amateur teams when a powerful lightning bolt struck near the players on the field. According to local authorities, 24-year-old Sofwan Awae suffered serious injuries from the strike. Emergency responders rushed to provide medical assistance, but despite efforts to save him, he later died. Police officials confirmed the tragic outcome and said that medical teams attempted to revive him following the strike. Video footage from the match reportedly showed the terrifying moment when lightning flashed across the field. Players were seen reacting instantly as the strike occurred, with several teammates rushing toward Awae to provide help. The sudden explosion and bright flash shocked everyone present at the stadium. Several other footballers were also affected by the strike. Authorities said that around 12 players suffered injuries and were taken to hospital for medical treatment. One of those injured was reportedly a Malaysian player who was participating in the local tournament. Sofwan Awae was not only a player in the community tournament but also a rising football talent. He played as a winger for SAMCOLTS and had recently signed with Yala FC, a Thai third-tier football club. His death has caused sadness among teammates, supporters, and the wider football community. Yala FC expressed condolences to Awae’s family, describing him as a new member of the club and sharing sympathy with those affected by his passing. Many supporters have also paid tribute to the young player, remembering his passion for football and his contribution to the sport. The tragedy has also renewed attention on lightning safety in Thailand. Lightning strikes are a recurring natural hazard in the country, especially during periods of heavy rain and thunderstorms. According to Thailand’s Department of Disease Control, hundreds of people were affected by lightning incidents between 2020 and 2024, with many losing their lives. Thailand’s tropical climate means thunderstorms are common, particularly during the rainy season. Outdoor workers, farmers, athletes, and people taking part in outdoor activities are often among those most exposed to lightning risks. Experts advise people to avoid open areas during thunderstorms because lightning can strike the ground even when rainfall appears limited. Sports fields, agricultural land, beaches, and large open spaces can become dangerous locations during storms. Safety officials often recommend stopping outdoor games and activities when thunder is heard. Taking shelter inside a solid building or a fully enclosed vehicle is considered one of the safest options during lightning storms. Standing under trees is not recommended because trees can attract lightning and may cause serious injuries to people sheltering beneath them. The death of Sofwan Awae is not the first recent lightning-related tragedy in Thailand. Earlier incidents have also resulted in fatalities during sudden storms. In one case, lightning killed an engineering student and his aunt while they were inside a small shelter in Lampang province. In another incident, a pregnant woman in Uthai Thani province died after seeking protection under a tree during a storm. The danger of lightning is not limited to Thailand. On the same day as the football tragedy, lightning strikes in India’s eastern Jharkhand state reportedly killed at least 14 people, many of whom were agricultural workers outside in open fields. These incidents highlight the importance of greater awareness about extreme weather risks. While lightning strikes cannot be prevented, many deaths can potentially be avoided through better preparation, early weather warnings, and quick decisions to stop outdoor activities when storms approach. For sports organisers, the incident underlines the need for clear safety procedures. Matches and training sessions should be paused when thunderstorms are nearby, and players should have access to safe shelters. Amateur tournaments, where safety planning may sometimes receive less attention than professional events, can especially benefit from stronger weather monitoring systems. Football fans and communities around the world have expressed sympathy following the loss of Sofwan Awae. His death is a painful reminder that even a normal sporting event can become dangerous when nature changes suddenly. As climate patterns continue to create unpredictable weather conditions in many parts of the world, awareness and preparedness remain essential. Whether on a football field, a farm, or any outdoor location, recognising the warning signs of severe weather can help protect lives. Source: Reports from local authorities and international news coverage, including information published by The Independent and regional news agencies. Details are based on available reports at the time of writing and may change as further official information becomes available.

title: Disney Legends in Conversation: Eric Goldberg
summary: Eric Goldberg is an animator and director at Walt Disney Animation Studios, behind such characters as Genie, Mini Maui, and Louis.
body_text: Disney Legends in Conversation: Eric Goldberg Entertainment August 11, 2026 5 min. read The Disney Legends Award ceremony will mark the final day of D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event presented by Visa® , a one-of-a-kind, multi-day fan experience showcasing the very best in creative storytelling and innovation from across the worlds of Disney. Hosted by Ryan Seacrest , the event will be filled with tributes and unforgettable moments to honor and celebrate the icons behind the magic who have made a lasting impact on Disney. This year, The Walt Disney Company’s highest honor will be presented to 13 individuals — Chris Berman , Jerry Bruckheimer , Susan Egan , Eric Goldberg , Anne Hathaway , Bob Iger , Kim Irvine , Dwayne Johnson , the Jonas Brothers , Lin‑Manuel Miranda , and Alan Tudyk — who for generations have defined Disney across entertainment, storytelling, and experiences. In an exclusive Q&A, Eric Goldberg — who is being recognized in the Animation category — reflects on their contributions to the company and what it means to be named Disney Legends. How does it feel to be honored as a Disney Legend? I am very flattered and humbled to be included on this rare list of luminaries. To be included with so many people I admire is truly wonderful and moving. Which Disney films inspired you to become an animator? The first Disney film I ever saw was Dumbo , and it’s my favorite to this day. And, of course, I’m ancient enough to remember when Sleeping Beauty , One Hundred and One Dalmatians , The Sword in the Stone , and The Jungle Book first came to the movie theaters. I saw them all, numerous times! Was there an artist, collaborator, or mentor at Disney who helped shape your path? I was always a huge fan of [Disney Legends] Ward Kimball and Freddie Moore . Their animation always looked like it was enjoying itself on the screen. And, of course, no one compares with [Disney Legend] Mary Blair , the greatest animation designer ever. Genie from Aladdin is one of your most iconic characters. What makes him so unique? Well, you can’t mention the Genie without tipping the hat to the amazing [Disney Legend] Robin Williams , and part of what makes the Genie so unique is Robin’s abilities as an actor. Not only is he hysterically funny, but warm and sincere as well. I tried to develop movement for him — lightning quick attitude changes, the physical ability to mime whomever he was imitating — that reflected his puff-of-smoke flexibility. Out of all your characters and films, is there one you hold most dear? Definitely a “who is your favorite child” kind of question! It would probably be the Genie, but I love Phil , Louis , Mini Maui , the “ Rhapsody in Blue ” characters, the flamingo with the yo-yo, and all the others. You directed Pocahontas , along with Mike Gabriel, and a couple segments for Fantasia/2000 . What inspired you to branch out and explore other filmmaking roles? Frankly, and I hope this doesn’t sound obnoxious, it really wasn’t branching out. I consider everything I do as directing, including directing television commercials in the UK, starting in 1977. As a supervising animator on a feature, I’m directing the animators on the unit to make the character have a cohesive and unique performance. With feature directing, there are a lot more responsibilities, but the duties are very similar. The canvas just gets bigger! As the head of hand-drawn animation, you also mentor the next generation . Why is it so important to share your expertise — and what do you love about this medium? I feel, and my colleagues feel, that we must pass on what we know to future generations. We were all lucky enough to learn from masters of the craft, and we are impelled to keep this medium alive. I think the beauty of animation is that you can achieve practically anything, and there is nothing that compares to the exuberance and believability of an exceptional animated performance. Plus, I’m a geek on the stuff About the Disney Legends Program The Disney Legends Awards program is a 39-year tradition of The Walt Disney Company, which began when Fred MacMurray was honored in 1987. Including this year’s honorees, a total of 329 Disney Legends has been named. Past Disney Legends include Tim Allen , Julie Andrews , Angela Bassett , Tony Baxter , Kristen Bell , James Cameron , Jamie Lee Curtis , Miley Cyrus , Marc Davis , Robert Downey Jr. , Harrison Ford , Annette Funicello , Josh Gad , Whoopi Goldberg , Jonathan Groff , Steve Jobs , Elton John , Angela Lansbury , Stan Lee , George Lucas , Steve Martin , Burny Mattinson , Alan Menken , Idina Menzel , Hayley Mills , Fess Parker , Ellen Pompeo , Robin Roberts , the Sherman Brothers , Marty Sklar , Dick Van Dyke , Barbara Walters , Betty White , John Williams , Robin Williams , and Oprah Winfrey . title: Agent Plugin Support
summary: Resend now supports the Agent Plugins Standard.
body_text: Today, Resend Skills announces support for the Agent Plugins Standard , an open, vendor-neutral standard for packaging skills and MCP servers into a portable plugin. What is the Agent Plugins Standard? Two tools have become critical in agentic development: MCP: agent tools for accomplishing tasks Skills: domain-specific, opinionated expertise Many AI coding tools package these together in a plugin format. For instance, we launched our Claude Connector and Codex Plugin . These plugins package together the MCP and agent skills in one simple install, and yet each one expects a different vendor-specific manifest, folder structure, and setup process. Agent Plugins is a vendor-neutral plugin format that provides a simple, portable way to package MCP and agent skills for use with any AI coding tool , without a vendor-specific manifest required. How to use it Nothing changes for existing installs like Claude , Codex , and Cursor . Any other client that supports the Agent Plugins format can install both Resend Skills and the MCP server using the plugin.json config. Follow your AI client's instructions to install the plugin. For example, in VS Code: Open the Command Palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P or Cmd+Shift+P ) Type Chat: Install Plugin from Source . Paste https://github.com/resend/resend-skills in the input field. After install, the plugin will be available in your AI client with full support for all the Resend skills. When you first use the MCP server, you will be prompted to authenticate. At launch, Agent Plugins are supported in ChatGPT , Codex , Cursor , GitHub Copilot , Kiro , VS Code , Hermes , and OpenClaw . How does it work Every compatible client checks for plugin.json in the root of the plugin directory. The standard also allows a skills/ directory and/or mcp.json configuration file. my-plugin/ ├── plugin.json ├── skills/ │ └── summarize/ │ ├── SKILL.md │ ├── scripts/ │ └── references/ └── mcp.json plugin.json : defines the name, version, and details of the plugin skills/ : contains the plugin's skills, each following the Agent Skills spec mcp.json : defines the plugin's MCP configuration The standard was developed in a collaborative effort by Amazon, Cursor, GitHub, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel and is already supported by many AI clients. Conclusion We'll keep the vendor manifests and the Agent Plugins files in sync as the standard evolves. If you have any questions, please reach out to us and we'll be happy to help.

title: AWS IAM Identity Center makes management of AWS account access optional for new organization instances
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS IAM Identity Center makes managment of AWS account access optional for new organization instances
body_text: AWS IAM Identity Center now lets you decide whether to enable management of AWS account access when you create a new organization instance. This allows you to use IAM Identity Center to manage access to AWS applications only, without the need to manage access to AWS accounts. This feature is available at the time of initial configuration of an IAM Identity Center instance and does not affect existing IAM Identity Center instances. IAM Identity Center enables you to connect your workforce identities to AWS once and offer AWS application owners across your organization streamlined access management. Application end users benefit from single sign-on, user awareness, and consistent authentication experience across AWS applications. Previously, this meant you also needed to manage access to AWS accounts. With this release, account management is now optional. When you choose not to enable management of AWS accounts, IAM Identity Center does not provision its service-linked role into your member accounts, which reduces the access surface in your environment. You can enable account management permissions later through instance settings or the UpdateInstance API. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. To get started, see Configure instance settings in the IAM Identity Center User Guide.

title: 10 Mejores Universidades para Estudiar Enfermería en Chile (2026)
summary: Enfermería tiene un 93% de empleabilidad en Chile. Descubre las 10 mejores universidades para estudiarla en 2026, cuánto necesitas en la PAES y cómo prepararte para lograrlo
body_text: Descubre las 10 mejores universidades para estudiar Enfermería en Chile según sus puntajes de corte PAES 2026, acreditación y calidad académica. Guía actualizada para postulantes. ¿Tienes Enfermería en la mira para la Admisión 2026? Es una de las carreras de salud con mayor demanda y empleabilidad en Chile — con un 93% de inserción laboral al segundo año de egreso según datos del Ministerio de Educación. Hay opciones en prácticamente todas las regiones del país, pero no todas tienen el mismo nivel de exigencia ni la misma calidad formativa. En esta guía te presentamos las 10 mejores universidades para estudiar Enfermería en Chile , considerando sus puntajes de corte oficiales 2026, acreditación y lo que las hace destacar. Si quieres ver el listado completo de puntajes, revisa nuestro artículo de puntajes de corte Enfermería 2026 en Chile . ¿Qué criterios considera este ranking? Las universidades fueron evaluadas en base a: Puntaje de corte PAES 2026 (admisión regular, último seleccionado) Años de acreditación institucional y de la carrera Reputación académica y clínica Campos clínicos y hospitales asociados Empleabilidad y reconocimiento del título 💡 Tip: En Enfermería, los campos clínicos son fundamentales desde los primeros años. Antes de elegir universidad, investiga con qué hospitales y centros de salud tiene convenio cada programa. Las 10 mejores universidades de Enfermería en Chile 2026 1. Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile (PUC) Puntaje de corte 2026: 831.25 puntos Sede: Santiago La PUC lidera el ranking con el puntaje de corte más alto del país para Enfermería. Su Escuela de Enfermería forma parte de la Facultad de Medicina y está vinculada a la Red de Salud UC Christus, uno de los sistemas hospitalarios más avanzados de Chile. La formación combina una base científica rigurosa con práctica clínica temprana en centros de alto nivel. ¿Por qué elegirla? Excelencia académica, campos clínicos de primer nivel y un título con el mayor reconocimiento del sistema de salud chileno. 2. Universidad de Santiago de Chile (USACH) Puntaje de corte 2026: 813.55 puntos Sede: Santiago La USACH ocupa el segundo lugar con el segundo puntaje de corte más alto del país — dato que sorprende a muchos. Su programa de Enfermería tiene un enfoque marcado en salud pública y comunitaria, con campos clínicos en hospitales de la red pública de salud y una formación que prepara profesionales para trabajar en los contextos más diversos del sistema sanitario chileno. ¿Por qué elegirla? Arancel competitivo dentro del CRUCH, fuerte vocación de salud pública y un programa acreditado con alta empleabilidad en el sector público. 3. Universidad de Chile (UCH) Puntaje de corte 2026: 781.40 puntos Sede: Santiago La Escuela de Enfermería de la Universidad de Chile es una de las más antiguas e influyentes del país. Su programa combina una sólida formación científica con práctica en el Hospital Clínico de la Universidad de Chile y otros centros de la red pública, formando enfermeras y enfermeros con una visión crítica e integral de la salud. ¿Por qué elegirla? Historia, prestigio, campos clínicos de alto nivel y un título reconocido en todo el sistema de salud chileno. 4. Universidad Católica de la Santísima Concepción (UCSC) Puntaje de corte 2026: 768.70 puntos Sede: Concepción La UCSC es la mejor opción para estudiar Enfermería en la región del Biobío. Su Facultad de Medicina tiene una sólida tradición formando profesionales de la salud para el sur del país, con campos clínicos en hospitales y clínicas de Concepción y la región. ¿Por qué elegirla? Alternativa de alta calidad fuera de Santiago, con inserción laboral sólida en la macrozona sur y costos de vida más bajos que en la capital. 5. Universidad de Concepción (UdeC) Puntaje de corte 2026: 755.55 puntos Sede: Concepción La UdeC ofrece Enfermería en tres sedes (Concepción, Chillán y Los Ángeles), lo que amplía significativamente las opciones para estudiantes de la zona centro-sur. Su Facultad de Medicina tiene décadas de experiencia formando profesionales de salud, con campos clínicos en el Hospital Guillermo Grant Benavente — uno de los hospitales regionales más grandes de Chile. ¿Por qué elegirla? Tres sedes disponibles, campus universitario integrado y fuerte inserción en el sistema de salud de la macrozona sur. 6. Universidad Católica del Maule (UCM) Puntaje de corte 2026: 750.70 puntos Sede: Talca La UCM es la principal opción de alta calidad para estudiar Enfermería en la región del Maule. Su programa está acreditado y cuenta con campos clínicos en el Hospital Regional de Talca, lo que garantiza exposición a situaciones clínicas reales desde los primeros años de la carrera. ¿Por qué elegirla? Calidad académica acreditada, costos de vida menores y fuerte vinculación con el sistema de salud local. 7. Universidad de Los Andes Puntaje de corte 2026: 750.50 puntos Sede: Santiago La Universidad de Los Andes ofrece un programa de Enfermería con un sello humanista e integral muy marcado, que va más allá de la formación técnica para incluir componentes de ética, cuidado integral y acompañamiento al paciente. Sus campos clínicos incluyen la Clínica Universidad de los Andes. ¿Por qué elegirla? Formación humanista, énfasis en el cuidado integral del paciente y un ambiente académico exigente con grupos reducidos. 8. Universidad Católica del Norte (UCN) Puntaje de corte 2026: 746.95 puntos Sede: Antofagasta La UCN es la mejor opción para estudiar Enfermería en el norte de Chile.
